title: Survey-area weights changed northward trend estimates more in Northeast US fall trawls than in Bering Sea trawls in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested survey weighting in two public trawl records in 1982-2000 and 2001-2019. We kept fixed survey strata and fixed cohorts of 59 eastern Bering Sea taxa and 62 Northeast US fall taxa. Area weights changed estimated latitude trends by -0.46 and +0.27 km north per decade in the Bering Sea, and -2.98 and +6.38 in the Northeast. Only the late Northeast contrast excluded zero under eight-comparison corrected approximate intervals. A post-2008 step term changed that contrast to -3.75 km per decade with standard error 1.97. Thus the estimated weight effect depends on how the survey change is represented. Only the early Northeast area trend excluded zero in the four primary samples. The package gives code, source hashes, haul weights, taxon centroids, uncertainty and numerical checks. This is an audit of a distribution measure used in climate studies. It does not measure a climate or pollution effect. Cohort selection, catchability, survey boundaries and short periods limit inference.

display.caption: Taxon latitude indices and trends in fixed strata and fixed cohorts. Approximate HAC intervals use an eight-comparison correction. North is positive. The first five available years set each line reference.

Survey latitude and the taxon latitude contrast between area and unweighted estimates. The dashed line marks 2009. Area weights remove much of the shift in survey allocation. They cannot remove all change in catchability.
